{{Short description|German mathematician (1908 – 1975)}}
[[File:Toeplitz Hagemann Vieth Ulm Köthe 1930 MFO4233.jpg|thumb|According to the annotation of this photo by {{ill|Konrad Jacobs|de}}, it depicts [[Otto Toeplitz]], E. Hagemann, D. Vieth, H. Ulm, [[Gottfried Köthe]] in 1930.]]
'''Helmut Ulm''' (born 21 June 1908 in [[Gelsenkirchen]]; died 13 June 1975) was a [[Germans|German]] [[mathematician]] who established the classification of [[countable set|countable]] [[periodic group|periodic]] [[abelian group]]s by means of their [[Ulm invariant]]s.

==Career==

Helmut Ulm's father was an elementary school teacher in [[Elberfeld]]. After finishing high school in [[Wuppertal]] in 1926, he attended the universities of [[University of Göttingen|Göttingen]] (1926–1927), [[University of Jena|Jena]] (1927) and [[University of Bonn|Bonn]] (1927–1930), where he studied mathematics and physics, attending the lectures of [[Richard Courant]], [[:de:Erich Bessel-Hagen|Erich Bessel-Hagen]], [[Felix Hausdorff]], and the joint Hausdorff–[[Otto Toeplitz]] seminar. He graduated [[summa cum laude]] in 1930 with a thesis about countable periodic abelian groups (1933). In 1933–1935 he was an assistant in Göttingen and worked with [[Wilhelm Magnus]] and [[Olga Taussky-Todd]] editing [[David Hilbert]]'s ''Collected Works''. His [[Habilitationsschrift]] developed a generalization of the [[elementary divisor]] theory to infinite matrices, continuing ideas of Ulm's teacher Toeplitz.
It was submitted in Münster in 1936 and refereed by [[Heinrich Behnke]], [[Gottfried Köthe]], F. K. Schmidt, and [[B. L. van der Waerden]].  Ulm's promotion was delayed, apparently, due to his anti-[[Nazi]] views.

From 1935 until his retirement in 1974 Ulm worked at the [[University of Münster]], as an assistant, docent, and eventually professor (1968). Besides his three important papers on the classification of infinite abelian groups, Ulm published only a few notes in the proceedings of the Münster mathematical seminar, one of which dealt with solution of systems of linear equations by a computer. He suffered from poor health. During the [[World War II]], Ulm worked as a [[cryptographer]] at [[Pers Z S]] starting in August 1941 on a part-time basis from Thursday through to Saturday and on Monday through Wednesday at Münster.<ref name="crypt">{{cite journal |last1=Weierud |first1=Frode |last2=Zabell |first2=Sandy |title=German mathematicians and cryptology in WWII |journal=Cryptologia |date=6 June 2019 |volume=44 |issue=2 |pages=97–171 |doi=10.1080/01611194.2019.1600076 |publisher=Taylor & Francis |issn=1558-1586}}</ref> After the war he mostly taught courses in applied mathematics and supervised several Ph.D. theses; those of G. Tillmann (1952) and G. Roth (1961) were close to his old work on infinite-dimensional linear algebra and infinite groups.
